pages.title: CyTools_MeshStudio — architecture
pages.html:
CyTools_MeshStudio — architecture#

CyTools_MeshStudio replaces eleven Tools with one standalone application: specialised mesh operations, and complete workflows that chain them the way CyTools_LocalMesh chained its own pipeline. It is built on the CyToolsCore SDK 0.9.0 and follows Docs/StandaloneDelivery.md, Docs/MeshViewer.md and Docs/Localization.md of the SDK.

What it absorbs#

Absorbed Tool What comes over Where it lands
CyTools_AutoRemesher AutoRemesher 1.2.0 binaries, remesh remesh_auto, engine geometry
CyTools_QuadWild QuadWild Bi-MDF binaries, remesh remesh_field, engine geometry
CyTools_Xatlas unwrap, repack uv_unwrap, uv_repack, engine geometry
CyTools_Trellis2Texture inspect_mesh, generate_pbr mesh_inspect, texture_pbr, engine geometry
CyTools_TripoSR TripoSR weights and source image_to_mesh backend triposr
CyTools_SPAR3D SPAR3D weights and source image_to_mesh backend spar3d
CyTools_UniRig Articulation-XL weights and source mesh_to_rig
CyTools_LocalMesh TRELLIS.2-4B, DINOv3, BiRefNet, multivue photos_to_mesh
CyTools_ViewGenerator Zero123++, ControlNet, DINOv2, SAM 2.1 the views_* operations
CyTools_MeshConstruct SAM 2.1 large, Depth Anything, PerspectiveFields, Wonder3D, SyncDreamer construct_proxy, analyze_views
CyTools_WHAM WHAM source (its weights had never been installed; they are now) video_to_motion, video_inspect

Their weights were moved, not copied: app/scripts/migrate_assets.py performed 49.9 GiB of same-volume renames and wrote data/reports/migration-manifest.json, which rollback replays in reverse. The application sources of the eleven Tools are kept under runtime/legacy-apps/ so that every ported worker can be compared against its original.

Deduplication#

The point of the merge is to stop paying several times for the same thing.

  • Weights. Zero123++ v1.2 had been installed twice (MeshConstruct and ViewGenerator), 5.2 GiB each. The migration compared the two trees file by file and then by SHA-256 of unet/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors, found them identical, and kept one. The catalogue in app/models/catalog.json is now the single declaration of every model: 26 entries, 60.7 GiB, each with its engine, its backends, its licence and its revision.
  • Environments. The eleven Tools carried thirteen virtual environments totalling 73 GiB, most of them a different copy of the same PyTorch build. app/engines.json declares eight, grouped strictly by dependency stack — never by theme.
Engine Stack Backends
geometry Python 3.11, CPU, trimesh/xatlas + native binaries autoremesher, quadwild, xatlas, pbrbake, meshedit, proxyfit
torch-cu124 Python 3.11, torch 2.5.1+cu124 triposr, spar3d, unirig
trellis Python 3.12, torch 2.8.0+cu128, transformers 5.x trellis, birefnet
diffusion Python 3.12, torch 2.8.0+cu128, diffusers 0.35.2, transformers 4.57 zero123plus, mirror, sam2, depthanything, perspectivefields
wonder3d Python 3.10, torch 2.1.2+cu121, diffusers 0.19.3 wonder3d
syncdreamer Python 3.10, torch 2.1.2+cu121, pytorch-lightning 1.9 syncdreamer
wham Python 3.9, torch 1.11+cu113 wham
hi3dgen Python 3.10, torch 2.4.0+cu121, spconv 2.3.8, xformers 0.0.27, transformers 4.46.3, numpy 1.26.4 hi3dgen

Seven, not the six first planned: Wonder3D and SyncDreamer run the same torch build but need diffusers 0.19.3 with transformers 4.35.2 on one side, and pytorch-lightning 1.9 with transformers 4.37.2 and taming-transformers on the other. The install steps the absorbed Tool had validated said so; the merge was undone before it was built.

Three extensions of torch-cu124 have no wheel for this ABI and are compiled at install time (torchmcubes, texture_baker, uv_unwrapper). The installer downloads the official NVIDIA redistributables into runtime/cuda-12.4 and loads the MSVC toolchain into its own process: no driver is touched, the machine PATH is untouched, and no system CUDA installation is required. torch-scatter and torch-cluster come from the PyTorch Geometric wheel index.

A backend also declares the environment variables its upstream code expects (HF_HUB_CACHE, U2NET_HOME, ALPHA_CLIP_PATH…), and the host sets them before the process starts: huggingface_hub reads its cache path when it is imported, so a handler that sets it afterwards is already too late — which is exactly how TripoSR failed its first run here.

trellis and diffusion both run torch 2.8.0+cu128 and would look mergeable, but the LocalMesh engine needs transformers 5.17 with huggingface_hub 1.x while the diffusers 0.35.2 stack needs transformers 4.57 with huggingface_hub 0.36. Those are incompatible majors, so the two engines stay separate. torch-cu124 is the opposite case: TripoSR and SPAR3D shipped with transformers 4.42.3 / trimesh 4.4.1 and UniRig with 4.51.3 / 5.1.0; the merged engine pins the newer pair, and each of the three backends has to be executed here before it is declared supported. If one of them cannot be made to work on the shared pins, it gets its own engine and that is written down rather than hidden.

Runtime structure#

The façade, the CLI and MCP all submit to the same Runtime; there is no second scheduler. Heavy work never runs in the application process: each backend runs in a persistent worker process started with its engine's interpreter, speaking the JSON-lines protocol in meshstudio/engines/workerhost.py (handshake, streamed progress, log forwarding, cancellation by killing the process tree, idle unload). That host and workers/_protocol.py come from CyTools_AudioStudio, where the same problem was already solved; they are Tool-local infrastructure, not additions to the Core.

text
app/  CyTool.json          manifest: every operation, its schema, its backends  engines.json         the eight engine environments and their sources  tool.py              create_runtime + one handler per operation  setup_engine.py      builds one engine environment at its final path  meshstudio/          business package (paths, engines, catalog, mesh, workflow)  workers/             one worker per backend, run by the engine interpreter  gui/                 Dear ImGui interface: tools, workflows, installation, updates  desktop.py           graphical entry point started by the launcher  launcher.cpp         source of CyTools_MeshStudio.exe (build_launcher.ps1)  models/catalog.json  generated by scripts/build_catalog.py  models/install.json  what an absent model needs to become installable  updates.py           the three update streams, and the swap done at the next start  scripts/             migrate_assets.py, build_catalog.py, install_model.pydata/  inputs models jobs settings logs reports workflows presets libraryruntime/  python/              light application interpreter  engines/             the eight heavy environments  sources/             upstream engine checkouts, pinned by revision  natives/             AutoRemesher and QuadWild binaries  legacy-apps/         sources of the eleven absorbed Tools, for reference  downloads/ updates/ backups/

Operations#

Specialised operations keep the contract of the Tool they come from, so a client that drove the old Tool keeps its parameters. Workflows are the second half of the brief: a saved chain of operations (for example photos → views → mesh → remesh → UV → PBR → rig) applied to one input or to a folder, runnable identically from the interface, the CLI and MCP. A workflow is data, not code: it is stored in data/workflows and executed by the runner in meshstudio/workflow, which submits each step as a real job.

Models: catalogue, install plan, licensed files#

Two files describe the weights, and they answer different questions.

  • app/models/catalog.json is built by app/scripts/build_catalog.py and says what exists: every model, its family, its engine, its backends, its size, its revision when a receipt recorded one, its licence. It also lists a model that is declared but absent, so the interface can show what is missing instead of staying silent until a job fails.
  • app/models/install.json says how an absent model becomes installable. Each item is either automatic (downloaded and hashed by app/scripts/install_model.py, with a receipt in cytools-receipt.json) or manual.

A manual item is a file whose licence is accepted in person, such as SMPL_NEUTRAL.pkl. The application never downloads it and never asks for the credentials of those sites: it shows the page, and import_model_file puts in place the file the user obtained, after checking it really is that file. A worker whose weights are incomplete refuses before loading anything, so the error names the missing files and the page rather than failing inside a pickle.

The state shown by list_models and diagnose comes from the files on disk, crossed with the plan: a half-downloaded model reads Partial, never Installed.

Updates: three streams, one swap#

app/updates.py keeps the three apart because they change for different reasons:

  • the application is a GitHub release of the app folder — check, stage, verify, activate, roll back;
  • an engine is rebuilt from the revision pinned in app/engines.json by install_engine;
  • the weights follow the catalogue and the install plan above.

Staging never touches the running application: the archive is downloaded (or copied), hashed against the expected SHA-256 when one is given, unpacked under runtime/updates and verified — same tool id, no data/ folder, a complete tree. Activation only records the request in pending.json. The directory rename itself happens at the next start, performed by a separate process (runtime/updates/apply.py) before anything of the application is imported, so the folder holding the running code is never swapped underneath it; the previous app is kept under runtime/backups, and a rollback records the reverse move the same way. If the rename fails, the working folder is put back.

data/ is never read, replaced or removed by any of this.

Interface tests#

Two tests guard the interface, and both exist because a defect shipped without them:

  • app/tests/validate_forms.py draws every operation's form, one process per operation, with one entry pre-filled in each list of objects so the sub-form of an entry is drawn too. A form is generated from its schema, so a shape no widget supports only crashes when that operation is selected — rendering one form and calling the interface tested is how eight operations shipped with a seed slider that asserts inside Dear ImGui, and drawing those lists only while they were empty is how their sub-forms went untested.
  • app/gui/interaction_tests.py (--ui-test-interactions) drives the Dear ImGui test engine: it clicks every tool of the list, opens the advanced section of each, walks the tabs, adds and removes a workflow step, refreshes the installation report, and checks that a model that can be installed offers its button, that a licensed file shows its page, and that the updates tab reads the real version. It found a Remove button that was clipped out of its child window and never answered a click.

Run both after touching gui/, in English and with --ui-test-language=fr. They must not run at the same time: one runtime owns the data directory.

The parameter editor#

gui/widgets.py turns an inputSchema into controls, which is what keeps 36 operations usable without a line of UI written per operation. The shapes it handles, and why each one exists:

Schema Control
enum combo
boolean checkbox
number with minimum and maximum close enough slider
number otherwise, and every x-cy-kind: Seed typed field (a seed's range is wider than a Dear ImGui slider accepts) plus a Random button writing -1
x-cy-kind: File / Image / Video / Directory text field, Browse, Clear, with the filter of that kind
array of strings list with Add and per-item removal
array of objects one sub-form per entry, Add files (one entry per file chosen) and Add empty
object, or an array of anything else JSON box, the last resort

A file dialog is asynchronous, so the pending request carries a path — views_generate#images#1#file — and the answer is written at that exact place, including inside a list entry.

Verification rules#

Nothing is declared supported before it has been executed here. platforms[].tested entries are filled only from runs that actually happened on this machine, and the migration, the engine merges, cancellation, the model installer and the update flow each need their own evidence in data/reports. Linux has a launcher and instructions but no run on this machine, and is declared as such.

pages.title: Modular CyUI integration
pages.html:
Modular CyUI integration#

The standalone application uses CyUI 1.2.0, pinned to ff023e6.

Selected modules and replacements#

Core; Inspector; Viewport; Images; Canvas; Diagnostics.

  • Boolean, enum and exact integer/float operation parameters use Inspector, stable IDs and host revisions. Only commit events update submitted parameters.
  • The live PBR preview texture is presented by Viewport.
  • Structured logs use Diagnostics; character selection and complete file copy remain available.
  • Core replaces the old monolithic CyUI revision; the old cyui.json provenance record is replaced by the complete hashed source manifest.

Reproducible source and delivery#

app/cyui-source.json records every selected upstream file and its SHA-256. app/cyui.py and app/cyui_modules/*.py are unchanged official sources, normalized to LF. Do not edit them: host adapters live outside the library. Refresh only from the exact pinned checkout:

sh
python app/scripts/sync_cyui.py /path/to/CyUI

The sources are included with the application using its existing source-vendoring mechanism. Neither a developer checkout elsewhere on disk nor an editable pip installation is needed. There is one imgui-bundle renderer, at the version pinned in app/requirements.txt; no C++ umbrella, CMake demo/gallery, CEF, extra model, AI engine, NumPy installation or browser dependency is introduced by this migration. Existing application/DSP/rendering dependencies are kept where required.

Keep LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt with the product. The application's own license does not change. The Options licenses list identifies the upstream revision and source.

Host responsibilities and retained adaptations#

File pickers, nested schemas, mesh/PBR rendering, materials, scene presets, picking and six-axis orbit/free navigation remain host-owned. The shared viewport is deliberately used with navigation=False so its simpler orbit controller cannot remove the existing camera controls or impose a new zoom limit. Images/Canvas are only dependencies of this surface. The renderer keeps its existing moderngl/trimesh dependencies; CyUI supplies no 3D engine.

SDK operations, permissions, exclusive groups, temporary AI task files, model installation, licenses/acceptance, generation recipes and Undo remain host-owned. No CyToolsCore runtime or AI library is copied into CyUI. English remains the default and French the persistent selectable second language.

Verification#

40/40 native forms; 49 native interaction checks; 12-triangle GLB fixture in the live shared viewport; int64/configuration replacement integration tests.

Run the adapter tests from app/ with the private Python:

sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_modular_ui.py -v

They verify pinned-source integrity, bounded log refresh/redaction and native ImGui frames across five themes, both densities, EN/FR and scale 1.0/1.5/2.0, plus the application-specific data/edit routing. This simulated DPI check is not a physical multi-monitor test. Windows native views are tested locally. Linux/macOS remain unverified by this migration; the source integration stays platform-independent.

Windows packages include the migrated sources and their license notices.

Final local results: runtime 5 passed; update fixtures 28/28; workflow fixtures 80/80; quad UV test 11/11 in the existing geometry engine; adapter tests 5/5; native forms 40/40 and interactions 49/49. Boolean, enum and exact integer/float operation parameters use Inspector, stable IDs and host revisions. Only commit events update submitted parameters. The live PBR preview texture is presented by Viewport. Structured logs use Diagnostics; character selection and complete file copy remain available. Core replaces the old monolithic CyUI revision; the old cyui.json provenance record is replaced by the complete hashed source manifest. Reproducible source and delivery # app/cyui-source.json records every selected upstream file and its SHA-256. app/cyui.py and app/cyui_modules/*.py are unchanged official sources, normalized to LF. Do not edit them: host adapters live outside the library. Refresh only from the exact pinned checkout: sh Copy python app/scripts/sync_cyui.py /path/to/CyUI The sources are included with the application using its existing source-vendoring mechanism. Neither a developer checkout elsewhere on disk nor an editable pip installation is needed. There is one imgui-bundle renderer, at the version pinned in app/requirements.txt ; no C++ umbrella, CMake demo/gallery, CEF, extra model, AI engine, NumPy installation or browser dependency is introduced by this migration. pages.title: Task files — SDK 0.9.0
pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Task files — SDK 0.9.0#

SDK sessions are temporary by default. A task can contain several jobs; completion of one producer must not delete results needed by consumers. Models, application code, shared installation caches and the original source files are never task artifacts.

Tool implementation (mandatory)#

Configure the accepted input root once in create_runtime, before starting:

python
runtime.configure_inputs(DATA / 'inputs', fields={    'image_to_mesh': ['image_file'],    'synthesize': ['references.*.audio'],})

Use the same root as the existing input resolver (including any configured environment variable). Declare every input-file field, including nested array fields. These fields accept absolute external paths; the SDK copies the source into a unique task-owned subdirectory of the accepted input root before calling the handler. Existing relative paths are also copied. A model path, LoRA, export destination or executable is NOT an input artifact: do not declare these in fields. Keep file format/size validation in the handler. The shared import bundle limit defaults to 8 GiB, configurable by the Tool. All generated files, intermediate files and worker diagnostics MUST use JobContext.path. Never write generated media into a global directory. Explicit user saves (profiles, model registration, installation) remain persistent operations.

AI / MCP use#

  • Call operations with an absolute input path directly; no shell copy is required.
  • Or call cy_import_file({"source":"D:/project/image.png"}). The Tool process copies it and returns path (absolute), relativePath, SHA256 and size. Supply path to the operation. OBJ/MTL/textures and GLTF/BIN references are copied automatically. Additional files can be passed as companions, relative paths from the source directory; directory structure is preserved. Import the bundle before submitting it. This never downloads a model.
  • Poll cy_get_job; read/consume the results while the task remains open.
  • To preserve a result, use cy_export_job({"jobId":"...","destination":"D:/project/results"}). This copies the job bundle, including supporting files, into a unique destination directory outside the runtime; returned output paths point to the exported copy.
  • Call cy_finish_task({}) after all consumers finish. It removes imported copies AND whole job workspaces: generated results, intermediates and logs. It never removes the original files or the explicit exported bundle. An active worker returns Busy; cancelRunning:true requests cancellation and defers deletion until workers stop.
  • Disconnect also finishes all connection-owned tasks. A forgotten idle task expires after 3600 seconds by default. cy_keep_task_alive renews it; active workers are never removed by expiration. cy_begin_task accepts retentionSeconds (1..86400). Its returned sessionId can be passed to operation envelopes and task controls for concurrent task graphs. Finish each Tool's task only after downstream consumers have imported or consumed its output. Paths between machines require a transfer transport; a local path refers to the Tool's host.

SDK equivalents: CreateSession, ImportFile, SubmitJob, ExportJob, FinishTask, KeepTaskAlive; same authenticated ownership in JSONL and HTTP. Native Python:

python
with runtime.task(actor) as session_id:    job = runtime.submit(actor, session_id, 'image_to_mesh', {'image_file': source})    result = runtime.wait(actor, job['jobId'], timeout=300)    saved = runtime.export_job(actor, job['jobId'], destination)

The context manager closes on exceptions as well. Normal runtime shutdown cleans remaining temporary tasks. On restart, recorded temporary tasks are recovered for cleanup; recorded live worker processes block deletion. A redirected workspace or a locked file produces cleanupError and retries, never an unsafe recursive deletion. Do not claim that an OS-denied source can be read: the MCP must return a useful error.

Standalone and compatibility#

Interactive UI sessions MUST explicitly use temporary=False; their generated results remain available after closing the UI. Imported working copies still disappear on session/runtime close. CLI invoke and saved-configuration replay remain persistent for backwards compatibility. AI automation should use task sessions via SDK/MCP. Pre-0.9 sessions have no temporary flag and are preserved; there is no destructive migration of old inputs/results. Small SQLite job/session history remains, with the parameters and output payload removed for purged jobs (artifactsDeleted:true). Model weights and secrets must not be put into a job workspace or export bundle.

Verification required before delivery#

Test external image/audio/video/mesh inputs without manually placing them under the Tool; assert the real resolver accepts the staged path. Test bundles, failed/cancelled jobs, disconnect, expiration, exports, client isolation and a worker still running. Verify every configured file field, not only one selected Tool. A transport test is not proof of a new full AI inference run; report the distinction explicitly.

pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Tool delivery checklist#

Follow StandaloneDelivery, FullOperationAccess and TaskFiles before delivering a Tool.

  • Validate the manifest and execute its automated tests.
  • Launch the standalone from outside its installation folder; verify English/French, configuration persistence, copyable logs and every exposed business operation.
  • Exercise CLI and real MCP calls, including external inputs, result export, cancellation and task cleanup after workers stop.
  • Validate real model inference separately from synthetic transport tests.
  • Record the executed platform, model revision, output format and resource measurements.
  • Keep machine-specific reports under the Tool's data/reports directory.
  • State untested platforms and operations explicitly. A scaffold alone is not a delivery.

pages.title: Unreal integration
pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Unreal integration#

CyUEMCPSDK adapts CyToolsCore contracts to Unreal plugins. Follow its Docs/Integration.md and Docs/UpdateExistingPlugin.md. For an existing plugin, embed and adapt the C++ sources into its existing modules; the separate reference plugins are development examples, not mandatory dependencies. The Python companion uses CyToolsCore without copying its runtime or schemas.

Authentication, jobs, permissions and temporary task files retain the Core contract. Unreal assets integrated into a project remain persistent project changes. Provider transports are included in the SDK; CyAIConnectorLab is not a dependency. External MCP access and embedded assistant tool access require separate integration and validation. See the SDK validation guide for Windows Editor 5.3–5.8 coverage.

The optional Unreal assistant can ship one offline ZIP containing portable Python, its official Core wheel and companion dependencies. Follow the SDK's Docs/AssistantRuntime.md: background detection, explicit first-use installation, shared user storage by default and optional plugin-local storage. Only immutable, compatible bundles are shared; plugin sessions, settings and task files stay isolated. This assistant-specific policy does not change private Python environments for inference CyTools.

Validation#

Run from the repository root with Python 3.11 or newer:

powershell
python -m pip install -e ".[mcp,dev]"python -m pytest -qpython -m build --no-isolation

The automated suite covers schemas, authentication and ownership, concurrent scheduling, worker cancellation, resource reservations, HTTP/MCP, automatic input staging, temporary task cleanup, export, shared downloads, configuration and desktop scaffolding. Inspect wheel and source archive contents; schemas, templates and guides are required.

Optional .NET interoperability: dotnet build Examples/DotNetClient, followed by python scripts/validate_dotnet.py. The GitHub workflow defines Windows/Linux/macOS and Python 3.11/3.12 jobs. A local Windows pass does not certify the other platforms. Resource-capacity tests use fixtures; they do not establish model inference quality or GPU capacity for third-party Tools. Those need their own delivery evidence.

pages.title: Workflows
pages.html:
Workflows#

A workflow is a chain of operations of this Tool, stored as JSON in data/workflows and run identically from the interface, the CLI and MCP. It is data, not code: run_workflow reads the document and calls the same handlers a client would call one by one.

This page also records what the LocalMesh pipeline taught us, because the first real workflow of this Tool is that pipeline, opened up.

What LocalMesh did, and what it cost to learn#

Engine.generate() chained twelve stages in one call: load, read the reference, cut the subject out, measure the two profiles, sample the shape, clean the mesh, texture, finish, repad the atlas, orient and scale, export, render a thumbnail. The tier recipe (draft / standard / high / max / extreme) decided the pipeline type, the three step counts, the sampler, the atlas size, the triangle budget and the guidance, in one table.

Several of its behaviours are not preferences, they are incidents that were paid for, and any workflow built on top of it has to keep them:

  • A progress bar never goes backwards. Two emitters were fighting: the bar reached 45 %, fell back to 20 %, climbed again. The invariant is held in one place, and a stale tick is dropped — but never its cancellation check.
  • A shape too heavy is refused before it saturates the card. A multi-view job at the Standard tier produced 12.3 M faces and killed the display driver (BSOD 0x116). Above the ceiling, the job restarts at the lower tier instead of failing, and says so in a note.
  • VRAM is measured at the card, through NVML. The o_voxel wheel allocates raw CUDA outside PyTorch's allocator: the manifests announced 2.07 GB where the driver read 5.6.
  • Cut-outs are framed together. Framing each view on its own scales an elongated object differently per view — 37.9 % apart between a motorbike's profile and its front — and the fusion then thickens it.
  • Angles are measured, not assumed. A view filed as "left" was really at −53.6°; projected at −90° it carved a cavity in the back of the subject.
  • A measurement that cannot be trusted is refused. Over 30° of elevation, or the two heads disagreeing by more than 15°, and the round angles are used instead.
  • No WebP in the delivered glTF. EXT_texture_webp is all-or-nothing: Unreal refused the whole file, geometry included.
  • Stage previews are deleted once the model is written — they were 85 % of the library.

The shared front end#

Four of the absorbed Tools carried their own background remover (BiRefNet, u2net, transparent-background, SAM 2.1) and three estimated the camera differently (Depth Anything 3, DINOv2 + SAM 2.1, PerspectiveFields). prepare_subject does it once and writes a subject set:

text
outputs/subject/  front.png right.png left.png back.png   cut-outs, one common scale  contact.png                             contact sheet  subject.json                            what was measured

subject.json carries, per view, its source, its size, the framing geometry and its measured azimuth when the measurement was accepted; and, for the set, the camera report with refusedBecause when it was not. A reconstruction step consumes the folder through subject_set, so the subject is segmented once for the whole workflow.

The refusal is surfaced rather than silently swallowed: "the back view measures 32.7 degrees of elevation, over the 30 degree limit" tells the artist to re-shoot at eye level, where "round angles used" alone would not.

Measured on this machine: prepare_subject 8.7 s for four views, then photos_to_mesh 96.2 s at the draft tier, 77 370 faces, 4.31 GB peak VRAM — 105 s for the chain.

Feeding a step from another#

A step names where its input comes from:

  • input_from — the step whose output it reads (empty: the previous step, or the workflow input for the first one).
  • input_field — which output field of that step to take (empty: the main mesh output).
  • input_to — which parameter of this step receives it (empty: the field that operation normally reads its input from). This is what lets a step consume a prepared subject folder instead of a mesh file.
json
{"id": "mesh", "operation": "photos_to_mesh", "input_from": "subject", "input_field": "subject_set", "input_to": "subject_set"}

A step that needs more than one thing lists the others in extra_inputs ({"from": "shape", "field": "file", "to": "detail_mesh"}); "from": "@input" names the file the workflow was started on, which is how a retopology gets its original texture back.

Every step's parameters are validated against the operation's schema, and completed with its defaults, before the step runs — exactly as a job submitted on its own. A misspelt parameter fails on the step that carries it, naming it, instead of inside a worker after the steps before it have been paid for.

What a folder means: input_mode#

each (the default) runs the whole chain once per file of the folder: a batch of meshes. For four photographs of one statue that is wrong — each would become its own subject, and the four-view mode would never see four views. together runs the chain once, and the first step receives every file as one list. prepare_subject then gives each photograph its role from its file name (front, right, left, back, or face, droite, gauche, dos; accents ignored); a photograph without a role becomes the front if there is none. The mode is saved in the document and shown under the input in the editor; run_workflow can override it.

When a step fails: continue_on_error#

Without it, a failed step stops the workflow. With it, the failure is listed in the report and logged as a warning, and the step hands on what it received — exactly what it does when it is switched off — so the chain goes on. The engine comparison relies on it (one engine failing leaves the others), and so does Mesh to game asset: an input with no UV texture to transfer still gets its quad mesh.

app/tests/test_workflow_inputs.py runs every one of them with stand-ins in place of the models, its steps validated against the manifest, with its optional steps off and then on.

Resident sessions#

Splitting a heavy pipeline into steps is only worth it if the steps can hand each other what they produced. Writing a TRELLIS volume to disk and reading it back would cost more than recomputing it, so a worker keeps the intermediates in memory under a session key (workers/_protocol.py, SessionStore): at most two sessions, least recently used evicted, everything dropped when the worker exits — which is also what a cancellation does, since the host kills the process.

The store and the protocol are in place. The TRELLIS steps that will use it — shape, clean, texture, finish — are not written yet: they are what makes "re-texture this shape with another seed" and "edit between shape and texture" possible, and they must reproduce the ceiling, the fallback and the metering listed above rather than quietly dropping them. Until they exist, photos_to_mesh runs the engine's own chain, which keeps every one of those behaviours.

Resources#

The steps of a workflow run inside the job that started it, one after another, so the job reserves the maximum of its steps rather than their sum (runner.estimate). A step that needs more than the job reserved is reported by the scheduler before anything starts.

The tier recipe ( draft / standard / high / max / extreme ) decided the pipeline type, the three step counts, the sampler, the atlas size, the triangle budget and the guidance, in one table. Several of its behaviours are not preferences, they are incidents that were paid for, and any workflow built on top of it has to keep them: A progress bar never goes backwards. Two emitters were fighting: the bar reached 45 %, fell back to 20 %, climbed again. The invariant is held in one place, and a stale tick is dropped — but never its cancellation check. pages.title: Local documentation (CyDoc)
pages.html:
Local documentation (CyDoc)#

The editable Markdown listed in sources.json remains the source of truth. build.py imports it into CyDoc with stable page IDs, local media, full operation schemas and a lexical index of the shipped app/tool.py. Original French guides are retained; absent translations are explicit and tracked. Do not hand-edit app/help.

From the application root (Node.js >=22 and npm are build requirements only):

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en

--install installs the locked generator under runtime/documentation-build, outside the shipped application. Subsequent builds need no installation. An already built CyDoc checkout/package may be selected with --cydoc-root PATH.

The complete generated app/help/ is shipped with application/update archives. Open app/help/index.html through a file URL. F1 opens contextual help; Options provides manual and workspace buttons. No HTTP server, CDN, network request or Node.js is needed for reading. External reference links remain optional external navigation.

CyDoc is pinned in cydoc-source.json and distributed under MIT; its full notice is in this directory, app/help and root LICENCES. Preserve generated third-party notices. MeshStudio alone includes an original procedural GLB with the mesh module and Three.js. Other modules are selected from actual imported media. Unused module scripts are absent. No interactive graph, GIF decoder or video player is added merely because an application can produce that format.

Review app/help/migration-report.json for old/missing links and translation-report.json for missing/stale translations. SDK reference pages are labelled separately from actual application capabilities. Linux/macOS launchers remain unverified unless a validation report records an execution on those platforms.

pages.title: CyDoc migration validation
pages.html:
CyDoc migration validation#

Scope#

Existing user/developer guides, local illustrations, shipped operation schemas and the public Python entry-point source were migrated. The original Markdown is retained as editable source and for GitHub links. App/help is generated and includes all reader resources. Node.js is required only for regeneration; the reader uses local classic scripts and file URLs.

Checks executed on Windows#

  • Pinned CyDoc 0.1.0 built from revision 774f2a7eabf7dd181a98ffc5add115b580b67f42.
  • App-local npm lockfile installation and full CyDoc build/check.
  • Python routing tests: English/French, legacy paths, Unicode, spaces/hash characters, media links, unknown page fallback, browser failure, active operation and common anchors.
  • Native ImGui test-engine clicks on both help buttons and F1, using the product interpreter. The browser call was intercepted to assert its file URL without launching tabs.
  • The full standalone Options window was opened and closed in an isolated application copy.
  • Generated reader tested in a DOM fixture with network calls forbidden: rendering, operation links/anchors, language switch and in-window image expansion/Escape when used.
  • The pinned CyDoc core, interactions and packed-asset suites passed (25 tests), including keyboard/pointer controls and reading-position restoration.
  • Distribution selections are checked for the entire help tree and notices.

Limits#

The automation browser blocks file URLs. A real browser visual check of file-origin storage, layout, codecs and WebGL remains necessary; DOM fixtures do not prove it. Linux and macOS were not executed. Touch-device behavior is covered by library interaction fixtures, not a physical touch-device run. Existing missing translations remain visible in translation-report.json. No model inference was needed or rerun for this migration. The migration report records old missing references; SDK reference documents may describe older SDK releases and are explicitly labelled separately from current operation contracts.

Regenerate and verify#

From the application root:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en --print-url

Existing release builders regenerate/validate the manual before packaging. When a builder uses git archive, commit the generated reader together with its source changes first. Keep the complete app/help directory and LICENCES/CyDoc-MIT.txt in the delivered product.

The procedural GLB was decoded from its packed local provider without fetch: two PBR meshes, 15,744 triangles. GPU rendering in the documentation reader remains part of the real-browser check.

pages.title: CyTools_MeshStudio — developer notes
pages.html:
CyTools_MeshStudio — developer notes#

The user-facing guide is ../LISEZ-MOI.md; the design is in Docs/Architecture.md and Docs/Workflow.md; what was actually executed is in ../data/reports/VALIDATION.md.

What the repository carries and how to rebuild runtime/ from a clone is in ../README.md; data/reports/ is not versioned. The licences of everything fetched at installation are in Docs/ThirdPartyNotices.md (scripts/build_notices.py).

Built on the CyToolsCore SDK 0.10.1 (MIT), installed by requirements.txt from a pinned commit of its repository; its licence text is ../LICENCES/CyToolsCore-MIT.txt and the scaffold's notice LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt. The application process only validates, schedules and reports: every model and every native program runs in a worker started with the interpreter of its engine (engines.json). There is one Runtime behind the interface, the CLI and MCP.

Layout#

text
CyTool.json           generated — never edit by hand, see build_manifest.pybuild_manifest.py     rebuilds the manifest from the absorbed Tools' schemas + the new opslegacy-manifests/     the manifests of the eleven absorbed Tools, read by build_manifest.pyengines.json          the seven engine environments, their sources and their pinssetup_engine.py       builds one engine environment at its final pathtool.py               create_runtime: registers every handler, then run_clidesktop.py            graphical entry point started by the launcherupdates.py            the three update streams; also runs as `--apply` at the next startmeshstudio/           paths, engines, backends registry, operations, workflow runnerworkers/              one worker per backend, run by that engine's interpretergui/                  Dear ImGui panels: tools, workflows, installation, updatesmodels/catalog.json   generated by scripts/build_catalog.pymodels/install.json   what an absent model needs to become installablescripts/              migrate_assets.py, build_catalog.py, install_model.py, update_locales.py,                      build_notices.py, build_release.pytests/                forms, interactions, MCP, cancellation, updates

Release archives#

runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\build_release.py builds, from a committed tree (--ref, default HEAD), the two archives a GitHub release carries: -app.zip, git archive of the commit restricted to app/, LICENCES and the guides (an archive holding data/ is refused by the updater), plus the SDK wheel built from the pinned source in app/wheels, which the Updates tab stages; and -windows-x64.zip, the whole committed tree under a top folder plus the launcher compiled with MSVC, an embeddable CPython with the application's packages, uv and the native programs, each pinned by URL and SHA-256 in the script and recorded in runtime/RELEASE.json inside the archive. Nothing from this machine's runtime/ goes into them, and neither the engines nor the weights: what .gitignore keeps out of Git stays out of the release by construction.

After changing anything#

powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\build_manifest.pyruntime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app\CyTool.jsonruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\update_locales.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\test_tool.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tests\test_updates.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tests\validate_forms.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\desktop.py --ui-test-interactionsruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\desktop.py --ui-test-interactions --ui-test-language=fr

Never run two of them at the same time: the SDK gives the data directory to one runtime at a time, and the second start refuses (with a message box, not silently).

update_locales.py --check must report 0 strings without a French translation. New strings go into scripts/update_locales.py (interface, fields, operation names and descriptions) or scripts/locales_fr_parameters.py (parameter tooltips).

Command line and MCP#

powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py create-client --name "Dev" --permission filesystemExternal --permission network
powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke diagnose --params "{}"
powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py --data-dir data\jobs mcp

An MCP client launches that last command with absolute paths. --timeout matters for the long operations: the CLI defaults to 300 s, while the interface submits without a deadline.

Rules kept here#

  • Nothing is declared supported before it has been executed on this machine; platform-tested.json is filled only from real runs and build_manifest.py copies it into the manifest.
  • An operation that cannot work says which engine or which model is missing, and names the page when a licence must be accepted in person. No operation pretends.
  • data/ is never replaced by an update, and weights are never deleted to tidy up.
  • The Core is not modified: what is missing from the SDK is implemented here, in the Tool.

Application icon#

The logo source is assets/branding/logo.png. build_icon.ps1 derives the 16-256 px Windows ICO and assets/app_settings/icon.png for Hello ImGui. build_launcher.ps1 embeds the ICO in the launcher. branding.py selects assets independently of the working directory and assigns this Tool its own Windows taskbar identity.

Modular CyUI#

The standalone interface uses the pinned, selected CyUI 1.2 modules. See the migration and validation notes for replacements, retained host adaptations, source hashes and reproducible refresh instructions.

pages.title: CyTools_MeshStudio
pages.html:
CyTools_MeshStudio#

Maintenance: Cyberalien.

One desktop Tool for meshes: reconstruction from pictures (LocalMesh / TRELLIS.2, Hi3DGen, TripoSR, SPAR3D), generated and prepared views, quad remeshing (AutoRemesher, QuadWild), UV unwrapping, PBR texturing, mesh editing and inspection, rigging (UniRig), motion from video (WHAM), and workflows that chain all of it. It runs as a Dear ImGui application, as a command line, and as an MCP server, on the same CyToolsCore runtime.

The user guide, in French, is LISEZ-MOI.md. The developer notes are in app/README.md, the design in app/Docs/Architecture.md and app/Docs/Workflow.md.

Only Windows 10 with an NVIDIA card has been executed. The Linux launcher exists and has never been run.

Screenshots#

The standalone interface in English (version 0.1.3). Click an image to view it at full size.

Interactive 3D viewer — orbit and free-camera navigation, scene presets and studio lighting. The mesh shown here is a procedural demonstration object, not an AI reconstruction.

Reconstruction workspace — browse the mesh operations and configure image inputs, quality, seed and GPU selection. Engines and model weights are installed separately.

PBR baking — configure texture resolution, UV handling, metallic and roughness channels, alpha and GLB export.

What this repository contains, and what it does not#

The repository carries the application (app/), the shipped workflows and the small test fixtures (data/workflows/, data/inputs/), the user guide, the Linux launcher and the licence texts (LICENSE, LICENCES/).

It does not carry:

  • model weights (data/models/, about 61 GiB): installed from the Installation tab or with install_model, from the plans in app/models/install.json. Several are under non-commercial licences, and some ask for a personal acceptance on their page; the application says which, and never asks for credentials.
  • runtime/: the private Python of the application, one environment per engine, the pinned upstream checkouts, the native programs, staged updates and backups. All of it is rebuilt with the steps below.
  • jobs, logs, settings, test reports (data/jobs/, data/logs/, data/settings/, data/reports/): produced on the machine. The CLI token lives in data/settings/.
  • the Windows launcher CyTools_MeshStudio.exe: compiled from app/launcher.cpp and attached to each release.

Binary release (Windows x64)#

Each GitHub release carries CyTools_MeshStudio-<version>-windows-x64.zip: unzip it into a folder with a short path (QuadWild fails in paths longer than about 240 characters, and the Tool says so instead of running it) and double-click CyTools_MeshStudio.exe. It holds the application, an embeddable CPython 3.12 with the application's packages, uv, and the two native programs of the geometry engine, so nothing has to be installed first (Windows 10 or later, x64). The engines and the weights are not in it: the Installation tab builds each engine environment and downloads the weights, tens of gigabytes in all, from PyPI, GitHub and Hugging Face. What the archive is made of — each part with its URL and SHA-256 — is in runtime/RELEASE.json inside it; the archives are built by app/scripts/build_release.py from the tagged commit.

The lighter CyTools_MeshStudio-<version>-app.zip holds the app/ folder and the guides of the commit, without data/: what an installed Tool downloads from its Updates tab, which replaces its app/ folder and nothing else.

From a clone#

Windows, PowerShell, from the folder of the clone. Step 1 was executed on the development machine in a fresh environment (the SDK from its repository, then this Tool's own tests with that environment); steps 2 to 5 are the commands that were run here, not yet replayed from a fresh clone on another machine.

  1. The application environment — CPython 3.12. app/requirements.txt installs the CyToolsCore SDK 0.10.1 (MIT) from the archive of a pinned commit of its repository; neither git nor a published wheel is needed:
powershell
py -3.12 -m venv runtime\pythonruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r app\requirements.txt
  1. The launcher, with the MSVC compiler (a "x64 Native Tools" prompt):
powershell
powershell -File app\build_launcher.ps1
  1. The engines, one private environment each under runtime\engines, with their pinned upstream sources (app/engines.json). The interpreters come from runtime\interpreters, the py launcher, or uv python install:
powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\setup_engine.py geometry

then torch-cu124, trellis, diffusion, wonder3d, syncdreamer, wham, hi3dgen. The Installation tab of the application does the same.

  1. The two native programs of the geometry engine are not downloaded by setup_engine.py yet. Unzip them so that these files exist:

    • runtime\natives\autoremesher-1.2.0\autoremesher.exe from autoremesher-1.2.0-win32-x86_64.zip
    • runtime\natives\quadwild-bimdf-v0.0.2\quadwild.exe from windows-binaries.zip

  2. The weights: Installation tab, or for one model:

powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke install_model --params "{\"model\":\"trellis2-4b\"}" --timeout 7200

Then double-click CyTools_MeshStudio.exe, or run runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\desktop.py.

Updates#

The Updates tab reads the releases of this repository — MrMybal/CyTools_MeshStudio, declared in the manifest and changeable in the tab — stages one, activates it at the next start and can roll it back; data/ is never replaced.

0.1.2: the interface#

0.1.2 redraws the desktop interface with CyUI, Cyberalien's Dear ImGui library: a sidebar replaces the tabs, the tool and workflow lists have a search field, forms are property tables with one primary action, and Options offer five themes and two densities. The operations, the manifest schema, the CLI, MCP and data/ are unchanged, and so is the SDK (CyToolsCore 0.10.1): an installation in 0.1.1 updates from the Updates page with nothing else to install. A former theme preference is mapped to the nearest new theme.

Updating from 0.1.0, and going back#

0.1.1 moves the SDK from CyToolsCore 0.9.0 to 0.10.1, now under the MIT licence, and adds the LICENCES folder. The operations, the manifest schema, the protocol and data/ are unchanged, and 0.1.1 runs on either SDK.

  • A fresh installation: the 0.1.1 binary archive carries the SDK 0.10.1 and LICENCES.
  • An existing binary installation: the Updates tab replaces app/ only, and the Tool keeps running on the SDK it was shipped with. To move its SDK too, install the wheel the update brings, from the folder of the Tool: runtime\python\python.exe -m pip install --no-index --find-links app\wheels "cytools-core==0.10.1". The embedded Python cannot build a package from source, which is why the wheel is shipped and why pip install -r app\requirements.txt is for clones only. The LICENCES folder comes with the full archive; an update brings the SDK's own notice as app/LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt. Engine environments are not relocatable: keep the folder rather than moving runtime/engines to a new one.
  • A clone: git pull, then runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r app\requirements.txt.
  • Going back: the Updates tab rolls app/ back to the copy it kept under runtime/backups; 0.1.0 runs on the SDK 0.10.1 too, so the SDK can stay. A clone goes back with git checkout v0.1.0 and the same pip install -r. Copies received under the earlier licence keep their terms.

Tests#

powershell
runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\test_tool.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tests\test_workflow_inputs.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tests\test_updates.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tests\validate_forms.pyruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\desktop.py --ui-test-interactionsruntime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\desktop.py --ui-test-interactions --ui-test-language=frruntime\engines\trellis\Scripts\python.exe app\tests\test_quadtex.py

Never run two of them at the same time: one runtime owns data/ at a time.

Licence#

Copyright (C) 2026 Cyberalien.

CyTools_MeshStudio is distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 only (GPL-3.0-only); the full text is in LICENSE. It is built on the CyToolsCore SDK 0.10.1, which is under the MIT licence, and its interface is drawn with CyUI, Cyberalien's Dear ImGui library, also under the MIT licence; neither changes the licence of this program.

The LICENCES folder holds the full licence texts of what is shipped — the SDK and CyUI and, for the Windows binary archive, Python, pip, uv, AutoRemesher and QuadWild — and LICENCES/SOURCES.txt gives the source of each.

You may redistribute and modify this program under the terms of its licence. It comes without any warranty, including the implied warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose.

The engines, upstream sources, native programs and model weights are fetched at installation, under their own licences — several of them non-commercial. They are listed in app/Docs/ThirdPartyNotices.md, generated from app/engines.json and app/models/catalog.json.

Modular CyUI#

The standalone interface uses the pinned, selected CyUI 1.2 modules. See the migration and validation notes for replacements, retained host adaptations, source hashes and reproducible refresh instructions.

CyUI: MIT. Full license: LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt. Upstream license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE Repository: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI (currently private; no upstream access required to run this application).

Local documentation#

Open Options → Open local manual (F1) or press F1 in the application. The complete offline reader is shipped in app/help/index.html. Regenerate the manual.

Internally converted to continuous angles. For Top/Bottom the in-plane orientation is searched automatically unless azimuth is given."            },            "azimuth": {              "type": "number",              "minimum": -360,              "maximum": 360,              "description": "Degrees around the vertical axis: 0 = camera in front of the object, 90 = camera on the object's right side, 180 = behind. pages.title: complete_subject
pages.html:
From one picture, generate the right, left and back views with Wonder3D around the vertical axis of the picture, then cut the four views out at one common scale: a subject set for the four-view path of LocalMesh. Only for a level front view: with a three-quarter or top view the generated views are tilted and the fusion deforms the object. The generated views are marked as such, and LocalMesh measures their angles itself.

pages.title: construct_proxy
pages.html:
Build a simple, clean, mostly hard-surface proxy mesh (lofted cross-sections, extruded polygons, boxes, cylinders) from one or several pictures of the same object, and project the pictures on it. AI models only supply masks, relative depth, camera poses and optional synthetic views.

pages.title: image_to_mesh_hi3dgen
pages.html:
Hi3DGen (Stable-X): the picture becomes a sharp normal map (StableNormal YOSO), and a TRELLIS v1 retrained on normal maps turns that normal map into a mesh. Geometry only, on a 256 grid, in the same frame as the LocalMesh output: texture it with "Texture a mesh for its own topology", or regenerate its detail on the 1536 grid first with "Refine a mesh". pages.title: texture_mesh
pages.html:
Give a remeshed model — QuadWild quads, a retopology, any mesh aligned with the reference — a texture made for that exact topology. "generate" asks TRELLIS.2 to generate it on this mesh from the reference picture, as LocalMesh does on its own mesh; "transfer" re-projects the texture of the detailed model instead, with no model. The detailed model, when given, is also baked into a normal map. Quads are kept in the OBJ; the GLB is triangulated, as glTF requires.

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see https://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see https://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see https://opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                    from                                compatible? (1)

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under

Thanks to the many outside volunteers who have worked under Guido's
direction to make these releases possible.

CyTools_MeshStudio - sources and licences of what is distributed
================================================================

This folder holds the full licence texts of the components shipped with the product.
A link or a licence name does not replace a text: each one below is in this folder.


CyTools_MeshStudio
------------------
Licence : GNU General Public License, version 3 only (GPL-3.0-only).
Text    : LICENSE, at the root of the product.
Source  : https://github.com/MrMybal/CyTools_MeshStudio
Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien.


CyToolsCore SDK 0.10.1
----------------------
The runtime, the scheduler, the transports (CLI, MCP) and the scaffold files in app/.
Licence : MIT. Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien.
Text    : LICENCES/CyToolsCore-MIT.txt (the same notice is kept as
          app/LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt, where the scaffold writes it).
Source  : https://github.com/MrMybal/CyToolsCore
Guides  : in that repository, README.md, Docs/CreatingYourFirstCyTool.md,
          Docs/Licensing.md and Docs/UpdateExistingProducts.md. The documents under
          app/Docs that describe the SDK are copies of its own.
Install : app/requirements.txt installs it from the repository, pinned to commit
          a8d200f2d0baaade1633e0683663b4506c595f74. The release archives carry the wheel
          built from that commit in app/wheels; its own copy of the licence is inside it.
The MIT licence of the SDK does not change the licence of CyTools_MeshStudio itself.


CyUI (Cyberalien's Dear ImGui interface library), Python port
-------------------------------------------------------------
The look of the desktop interface: palette, themes, fonts and widgets.
Licence : MIT. Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien.
Text    : LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt.
Source  : app/cyui.py is an unmodified copy of the library's python/cyui.py;
          app/cyui.json records its SHA-256 and the date of the copy, and
          app/scripts/sync_cyui.py refreshes both.
The MIT licence of CyUI does not change the licence of CyTools_MeshStudio itself.


Parts shipped only in the Windows binary archive
------------------------------------------------
CyTools_MeshStudio-<version>-windows-x64.zip adds the parts below to the application.
Their exact download URLs and SHA-256 are in runtime/RELEASE.json inside the archive.

CPython 3.12.10, embeddable distribution
  Licence : PSF-2.0.
  Text    : LICENCES/Python-3.12-PSF.txt (also runtime/python/LICENSE.txt).
  Source  : https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31210/

pip 26.2.1
  Licence : MIT.
  Text    : LICENCES/pip-MIT.txt
  Source  : https://github.com/pypa/pip

Python packages of the application (runtime/python/Lib/site-packages)
  Each package keeps its own licence in its *.dist-info folder; the Options tab of the
  application lists them with their licence.

uv 0.12.19
  Licence : MIT OR Apache-2.0.
  Texts   : LICENCES/uv-MIT.txt and LICENCES/uv-Apache-2.0.txt
  Source  : https://github.com/astral-sh/uv

AutoRemesher 1.2.0
  Licence : MIT.
  Text    : LICENCES/AutoRemesher-MIT.txt
  Source  : https://github.com/huxingyi/autoremesher
  The upstream Windows archive is redistributed unmodified. It bundles third-party
  libraries as its author packaged them: Qt 5, ANGLE, Intel TBB, the software OpenGL
  library shipped with Qt, and Microsoft runtime libraries, each under its own terms.
  Qt is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 3
  (LICENCES/Qt-LGPL-3.0.txt, which refers to the GPL text in LICENSE); its sources are

pages.title: Entrées locales automatiques
pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Entrées locales automatiques#

Une IA ou un utilisateur peut fournir directement le chemin absolu d'un fichier accessible au processus du Tool. Ne pas exiger de copie manuelle dans data/inputs. Le Tool importe automatiquement le fichier dans le workspace privé du job via :

python
snapshot = context.import_input(parameters['image'], base_dir=DATA/'inputs',                                suffixes=['.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.webp'],                                max_bytes=32*1024**2)

Transmettre uniquement le snapshot au worker. Valider le contenu réel sur ce snapshot avant son traitement (décodage image, dimensions, etc.). Les noms relatifs déjà utilisés restent résolus depuis base_dir. Un chemin relatif sortant du dossier est refusé ; l'appelant peut fournir le chemin absolu explicite du fichier externe.

Le SDK copie par blocs avec contrôle de taille et annulation, impose un fichier régulier, produit des noms uniques et écrit inputs/imports.json (source, taille, SHA256, snapshot). Le fichier original reste intact et deux jobs n'écrasent pas leurs entrées. Les entrées provenant des workspaces de ce runtime respectent la visibilité des jobs authentifiés. Les permissions de lecture du système d'exploitation continuent de s'appliquer. Aucun clientId métier ne choisit le propriétaire. Réserver le disque nécessaire aux copies dans l'estimateur du Tool et prévoir leur rétention avec celle du job.

Une chaîne locale réutilise donc directement le chemin retourné par le Tool précédent. Un fichier présent seulement sur un autre hôte nécessite un transfert préalable ; un chemin seul ne transporte pas ses octets. Ne pas télécharger arbitrairement une URL.

Le schéma d'entrée doit décrire les chemins absolus acceptés et l'import automatique. Le MCP, la CLI et le standalone appellent le même handler. Une fenêtre de sélection de fichier doit transmettre son chemin sans imposer une copie dans un dossier partagé. Tester une entrée hors du Tool (espaces/Unicode), des noms identiques, une modification de l'original, les limites de taille, le contenu invalide et l'isolation entre clients.

Depuis le SDK 0.9.0, utiliser aussi runtime.configure_inputs pour tous les champs de fichiers : import commun SDK/MCP et gestion de la tâche selon TaskFiles.md. Cette intégration couvre les 19 Tools livrés. import_input reste disponible pour les validations et snapshots privés du handler.

Durée de vie#

Les copies importées sont temporaires par défaut (keep=False), en MCP comme dans les autres modes. Le Core les supprime après le retour effectif du handler, donc après l'arrêt de son worker, sur succès, erreur et annulation. La provenance légère reste dans imports.json avec removed=true. Ce nettoyage de snapshot préserve l'original et les résultats du job. La fin de tâche supprime ensuite les résultats temporaires selon TaskFiles.md. Un handler ne doit pas retourner une copie temporaire comme résultat durable.

keep=True conserve la copie pendant le job/la tâche pour débogage/reproductibilité ; cette option ne la protège pas du nettoyage final d’une tâche IA temporaire. LocalMesh expose keep_input_copies (false par défaut) dans son schéma IA et ses réglages avancés. Les configurations enregistrent cette option, pas les octets des images. Le cycle de tâche 0.9.0 ajoute la purge des résultats, la déconnexion, l’expiration et la récupération au redémarrage ; les workers encore vivants empêchent la purge.

Task-owned files (SDK 0.9.0)#

Read Docs/TaskFiles.md (TaskFiles.md from this Docs directory). Configure input roots and all file fields for automatic imports; AI sessions are temporary by default. FinishTask removes imported copies and generated workspaces after workers stop; export wanted results first. Standalone sessions explicitly use temporary=False.

pages.title: Créer son premier CyTool
pages.html:
Créer son premier CyTool#

Installer le SDK comme indiqué dans le README. Les commandes suivantes supposent que l'environnement virtuel contenant le SDK est activé (.venv/Scripts/Activate.ps1 sous PowerShell ou source .venv/bin/activate sous Linux/macOS).

powershell
cytools new ./CyToolExample --name CyToolExample --id cy.tool.examplecd CyToolExamplecytools validate CyTool.jsonpython -m unittest -vpython tool.py describepython tool.py list-operationspython tool.py invoke echo --params-file params.json

Le générateur crée un Tool fonctionnel. params.json contient {"text":"Hello CyTools"}. L'invocation retourne un objet job avec state: Completed et outputs.text. Les paramètres passés dans un fichier évitent les différences d'échappement entre shells.

Ajouter une opération#

Dans CyTool.json, ajouter un objet dans operations avec id/name/description, inputSchema/outputSchema. Employer additionalProperties: false pour détecter les fautes de frappe dans les paramètres. Le manifest lui-même accepte des métadonnées inconnues pour permettre l'évolution du standard.

Dans create_runtime, écrire def operation(context, parameters) puis appeler runtime.register('operation_id', operation). Toute opération déclarée doit avoir un handler : le runtime refuse de démarrer sinon. La CLI et le catalogue MCP se mettent à jour automatiquement, sans écrire un outil MCP supplémentaire.

Consulter les sept opérations de cytool_test/__init__.py pour l'annulation, la progression et les erreurs.

Lancer en MCP#

Installer cytools-core[mcp] depuis le checkout ou le wheel. Configurer un client MCP stdio pour lancer l'interpréteur Python du Tool avec les arguments absolus :

json
{  "mcpServers": {    "cytool-example": {      "command": "C:/path/to/venv/Scripts/python.exe",      "args": ["C:/path/to/CyToolExample/tool.py", "--data-dir", "C:/path/to/data/mcp", "mcp"]    }  }}

Ce bloc illustre le format courant mcpServers ; l'emplacement et la syntaxe de la configuration dépendent du client. Ne pas écraser sa configuration existante. Le client découvre op_echo, appelle {"parameters":{"text":"Hello"}}, puis consulte cy_get_job avec le jobId retourné. Voir MCP.md.

Livrer#

Installer le wheel de CyToolsCore avec le Tool, ou référencer une version précise. Ne pas dépendre d'un chemin de développement privé dans la distribution finale. Le SDK livre des scripts console Python ; produire un .exe autonome avec son outil de packaging est une étape propre au Tool, à tester avec ses dépendances. La génération ne choisit pas de licence à la place du propriétaire du projet.

pages.title: Dépendances
pages.html:
Dépendances#

CyDependencyDescriptor : id, version, required, source, installed, path, executable, platforms. Les exigences globales sont runtimeRequirements ; chaque backend peut avoir ses propres dependencies. CanRun contrôle la présence d'un path de fichier ou d'un executable résolu dans PATH pour les dépendances obligatoires.

Un champ installed:true dans un manifest n'est pas une preuve et ne remplace pas la détection. La contrainte version documente la version attendue ; le Tool doit vérifier la version réelle via une commande fiable de son programme. Le Core ne devine pas la syntaxe de --version de tous les exécutables.

Diagnose expose machine et enregistrement des handlers. Appeler CanRun avec les paramètres exacts pour la vérification opérationnelle des ressources et dépendances. Un diagnostic métier détaillé (drivers, modèles, comptes) peut être une opération supplémentaire du Tool, décrite comme les autres.

Aucune installation système automatique. Les éventuels tokens de téléchargement ou API doivent être fournis par l'hôte, jamais enregistrés dans CyTool.json.

pages.title: Téléchargements
pages.html:
Téléchargements#

DownloadManager(root, timeout=30) gère des fichiers HTTPS indépendamment du fournisseur. Hugging Face, GitHub Releases et dépôts officiels personnalisés peuvent fournir leurs URLs et headers ; les politiques de comptes, dépôts privés et licences appartiennent à l'adaptateur de la source. Le Core ne contourne aucun accès gated.

python
manager.download('weights.bin', url, sha256=expected_sha256, size=expected_size,                 headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token},                 license_accepted=accepted,                 pause=pause_event, cancellation=cancellation_token,                 progress=lambda downloaded, total: None,                 revision=repository_revision)

Le fichier partiel .part et ses métadonnées .download.json sont persistés. La reprise utilise Range et If-Range/ETag quand possible. Un serveur qui renvoie 200 au lieu de 206 entraîne un redémarrage propre du fichier ; une plage incohérente ou un ETag changé dans une réponse partielle est refusé. Sans ETag ni SHA256 attendu, le téléchargement repart de zéro pour éviter de mélanger des versions.

Pause retourne l'état Paused ; rappeler download avec les mêmes informations reprend, y compris après redémarrage de l'application. Une annulation interrompt la lecture, conserve le partiel pour reprise ; remove supprime les fichiers du nom concerné. Le timeout borne une attente réseau, pas une durée globale arbitraire de gros download. L'intégrité SHA256 et la taille attendue sont vérifiées avant le remplacement atomique du fichier final. verify permet une vérification ultérieure ; list_installed retourne les fichiers finalisés. Repair : vérifier puis relancer download avec le hash attendu. Update : fournir la nouvelle URL/révision et son nouveau hash, ou un nom versionné.

Les credentials sont uniquement en mémoire. Les redirections cross-host retirent Authorization/Cookie. Les URLs de téléchargement sont persistées : fournir une URL stable sans secret en query string. Un fichier hash-invalide est supprimé, jamais présenté comme installé. Les retries réseau sont explicites : le caller rappelle download, ce qui reprend le partiel conservé.

Le mode HTTP en clair est refusé, sauf allow_test_http sur loopback pour les tests. Un manager sérialise ses appels ; ne pas utiliser plusieurs managers concurrents sur la même destination. Le contrôle d'intégrité fourni par la source est fortement préférable à la seule taille ; ETag seul n'est pas une signature cryptographique.

pages.title: Erreurs
pages.html:
Erreurs#

CyToolError sérialise code, message, technicalDetails, recoverable et suggestedAction. Les codes restent des strings extensibles ; un client doit conserver un code inconnu. Les exceptions métier attendues ne doivent pas devenir des retours de succès ambigus.

Codes courants : InvalidDescriptor, IncompatibleVersion, InvalidParameters, InvalidOutput, MissingImplementation, UnknownOperation, MissingDependency, MissingRuntime, MissingModel, UnsupportedPlatform, UnsupportedBackend, InsufficientRAM, InsufficientVRAM, InsufficientDisk, UnsupportedCPU, AccessDenied, AuthenticationRequired, Busy, Timeout, Cancelled, Interrupted, WorkerCrashed, ProtocolError, DownloadFailed, IntegrityFailure, LicenseAcceptanceRequired, InternalError.

SubmitJob refusé retourne une erreur sans créer un job. Un handler qui échoue donne un job Failed avec error. Une lecture GetJob réussie d'un job Failed ne transforme pas l'opération en succès. Une exception inattendue du handler est InternalError.

Les détails d'erreur ou logs métier peuvent contenir des données utilisateur : le backend doit expurger les secrets avant context.log ou technicalDetails. Le Core ne prétend pas détecter tous les secrets arbitraires. L'API HTTP masque les exceptions internes du dispatcher en dehors des erreurs structurées connues.

pages.title: Événements et logs
pages.html:
Événements et logs#

Les événements contiennent sequence, type, timestamp, toolId, data et les identités clientId/sessionId/jobId lorsqu'elles s'appliquent. Le compteur est local à l'exécution du runtime ; il repart à zéro après redémarrage.

GetEvents(after) retourne les événements autorisés, cursor à transmettre au prochain appel et gap lorsque des événements demandés ont été évincés du buffer borné. Le client doit aussi réinitialiser son curseur si cursor devient inférieur au précédent. L'état de job persistant est la référence après perte d'événements.

Émissions V1 : ToolStarted/ToolStopping, SessionCreated/SessionClosed, JobCreated, JobQueued, JobWaitingForResources, JobPreparing, JobStarted, JobProgress, JobCancelling, JobCancelled, JobCompleted, JobFailed, ResourceReservationCreated/Released, Log. Les événements de modèles, previews, téléchargements ou connexions persistantes peuvent être ajoutés par leurs adaptateurs ; ils ne sont pas simulés comme preuves.

context.log(message, level) ajoute un log corrélé au job. Conventions de niveau : Trace, Debug, Info, Warning, Error, Critical. Le buffer en mémoire n'est pas une archive de logs durable ; un hôte peut exporter les événements dans son journal.
